title: Days of the Week and Times of the Day
seo_title: Foundation Time Worksheets: Days of the Week, Morning, Afternoon and Night (Free, with Answers)
standard_text: Sequence days of the week and times of the day including morning, lunchtime, afternoon and night time, and connect them to familiar events and actions.
meta_desc: Free Foundation (Prep, Kindergarten) maths worksheets on days of the week and times of the day, matched to the Australian Curriculum (AC9MFM02): morning, lunchtime, afternoon, night time, order of the day, yesterday and tomorrow. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: There are 7 days in a week, always in the same order.
key_sub: Morning, lunchtime, afternoon, night time. Yesterday is before today; tomorrow is after.
body_html:
Times of the day

A day has morning (we wake up and go to school), lunchtime (the middle of the day), afternoon (we go home) and night time (we go to bed).

Days of the week

There are 7 days in a week. They always go in the same order, then start again:

… Friday, Saturday, Sunday, then Monday again. Saturday and Sunday are the weekend.

Yesterday, today, tomorrow

Yesterday is the day before today. Tomorrow is the day after today.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do
Mixing up morning and afternoonMorning is before lunch; afternoon is after lunch
Saying the day before when the day after is askedAfter: count on one day. Before: count back
Thinking the week ends on FridayAfter Friday come Saturday and Sunday, then Monday

faq.q: What do Foundation students learn about time?
faq.a: They put the days of the week and the times of the day (morning, lunchtime, afternoon and night time) in order and connect them to familiar events (AC9MFM02). Reading clocks starts in Year 1.

faq.q: How can I help my child learn the days of the week?
faq.a: Sing a days-of-the-week song, talk about what happens on each day (library on Tuesday, sport on Friday) and mark the days on a family calendar.

faq.q: What is the difference between yesterday and tomorrow?
faq.a: Yesterday is the day before today and has already happened. Tomorrow is the day after today and has not happened yet.

faq.q: Why talk about the order of a day?
faq.a: Putting events in order (wake up, breakfast, school, lunch, home, dinner, bed) builds the idea that time moves forward and prepares children for clocks and calendars.

items.q: Which day comes after Monday?
items.e: The days go Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday, then Monday again. After Monday comes Tuesday.

items.q: Which day comes before Wednesday?
items.e: Count back one day from Wednesday: Tuesday.

items.q: Which day comes after Tuesday?
items.e: The days go Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday, then Monday again. After Tuesday comes Wednesday.

items.q: Which day is missing?
items.e: The days go in order: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday. The missing day is Wednesday.

items.q: How many days are in one week?
items.e: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday: 7 days.
